title: Nested generic models
body:
# Bug / Feature Request

Nested generic models seem to be significantly bugged, at least in 0.32.2 (I believe it's the same for 1.0?)

* OS: **Windows 10**
* Python version `import sys; print(sys.version)`: **3.7.3 (conda-forge)**
* Pydantic version `import pydantic; print(pydantic.VERSION)`: **0.32.2**

Tagging @dmontagu as per request from gitter.

It seems the direct issue I had in 0.30 doesn't exist, but I'm still unable to do what I wanted to do. 😛 

Ideally I would be able to set parametrized hierarchies of models using one generic TypeVar, and have them pick them up (as `OSet` below), similarly to `template<typename T>` in C++.

The way it currently works (`OUnset` and `OListNested` below) doesn't seem to support type checking, and doesn't support roundtripping in dicts at all (due to not knowing what to set in the generic type).

I would expect to be able to pass and "inherit" (for lack of better term in my knowledge) the same `TypeVar`s down the hierarchy of models, and enforce the concrete types. Also, it's strange that `OUnset` and `OListNested` work at all (though I guess X[T] is a subclass of X...), but I think that behaviour might be useful, as long as the caveats are documented.

Currently:

```py
>>> import sys
>>> import pydantic
>>> import typing
>>> from pydantic.generics import GenericModel
>>> print(sys.version)
3.7.3 | packaged by conda-forge | (default, Jul  1 2019, 22:01:29) [MSC v.1900 64 bit (AMD64)]
>>> print(pydantic.VERSION)
0.32.2
>>> AT = typing.TypeVar("AT")
>>>
>>> class InnerT(GenericModel, typing.Generic[AT]):
...     a: AT
...
>>> inner_int = InnerT[int](a=8)
>>> inner_str = InnerT[str](a="ate")
>>>
>>> class OUnset(GenericModel, typing.Generic[AT]):      
...     """This seems to work, allowing any InnerT[X]."""
...     i: InnerT  # just the generic
... # works:
...
>>> o_unset_int_int = OUnset[int](i=inner_int)
>>> # works, but might be unintuitive:
...
>>> o_unset_int_str = OUnset[int](i=inner_str)
>>> # Can't round-trip through dict due to not knowing the type
... 
>>> d_uii = o_unset_int_int.dict()
>>> d_uii
{'i': {'a': 8}}
>>>
>>> OUnset[int](**d_uii)
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
  File "C:\Conda\envs\bugs_pydantic\lib\site-packages\pydantic\main.py", line 275, in __init__
    values, fields_set, _ = validate_model(__pydantic_self__, data)
  File "C:\Conda\envs\bugs_pydantic\lib\site-packages\pydantic\main.py", line 785, in validate_model
    raise err
pydantic.error_wrappers.ValidationError: 1 validation error for OUnset[int]
i
  Type InnerT cannot be used without generic parameters, e.g. InnerT[T] (type=type_error)
>>> # IMO this should require InnerT[AT] instead of InnerT in
... # the definition (see OSet below)
... # -----------------
...
>>> class OListNested(GenericModel, typing.Generic[AT]):       
...     """This works (didn't in 0.30), but doesn't type-check."""
...     ii: typing.List[InnerT]
... # works:
... 
>>> o_list_int_int = OListNested[int](ii=[inner_int])
>>> # works, but might be unintuitive:
...
>>> o_list_int_str = OListNested[int](ii=[inner_str])
>>> # Still can't round-trip (same problem as OUnset)
...
>>> d_lii = o_list_int_int.dict()
>>> d_lii
{'ii': [{'a': 8}]}
>>>
>>> OListNested[int](**d_lii)
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
  File "C:\Conda\envs\bugs_pydantic\lib\site-packages\pydantic\main.py", line 275, in __init__
    values, fields_set, _ = validate_model(__pydantic_self__, data)
  File "C:\Conda\envs\bugs_pydantic\lib\site-packages\pydantic\main.py", line 785, in validate_model
    raise err
pydantic.error_wrappers.ValidationError: 1 validation error for OListNested[int]
ii -> 0
  Type InnerT cannot be used without generic parameters, e.g. InnerT[T] (type=type_error)
>>> # -----------------
... # Expected this to work and enforce the same type, like templates in C++.
... # But it produces an error due to InnerT[AT] as below.     
... 
>>> class OSet(GenericModel, typing.Generic[AT]):
...     i: InnerT[AT]
...
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
  File "<stdin>", line 2, in OSet
  File "C:\Conda\envs\bugs_pydantic\lib\site-packages\pydantic\generics.py", line 31, in __class_getitem__
    raise TypeError(f'Type parameters should be placed on typing.Generic, not GenericModel')
TypeError: Type parameters should be placed on typing.Generic, 
not GenericModel
>>> # This errors upon definition. Maybe premature erroring?   
... InnerT[AT]
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
  File "C:\Conda\envs\bugs_pydantic\lib\site-packages\pydantic\generics.py", line 31, in __class_getitem__
    raise TypeError(f'Type parameters should be placed on typing.Generic, not GenericModel')
TypeError: Type parameters should be placed on typing.Generic, 
not GenericModel
```

Expected:

```py
>>> # ...
>>> class OSet(GenericModel, typing.Generic[AT]):
...     i: InnerT[AT]
...     
>>> os_int_int = OSet[int](i=inner_int)
>>> os_int_int.dict()
{'i': {'a': 8}}
>>> OSet[int](**os_int_int.dict()) == os_int_int
True
>>> os_int_str = OSet[int](i=inner_str)
ValidationError: Type of `i` (inner_str) doesn't match OSet[int] (int != str).
```
